dissents.topic: Whether to keep a kw_only_dataclass helper or inline @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) at every call site

positions.position: Inlining 15 identical decorator stacks is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE; the helper was a named concept ('streamable, kw-only, frozen request type') and should be retained (minus the version branch) so future changes touch one place.
Keeping the helper (minus the version guard) would be the smaller, better patch — more characters and noise for zero clarity gained. Taste note, not a blocker.
Restore a thin helper to preserve the named project-wide convention; inlining loses the contract that streamable request types are frozen kw-only dataclasses.
Removing kw_only_dataclass was clean and good — does not call for restoring a helper.
Does not flag the inlining; treats the kw_only=True normalization as an improvement in readability.
Does not flag the inlining as a defect.

positions.position: P1 — either land the migration in this PR or file a tracking issue with an owner and deadline; bare TODO becomes permanent style debt.
P1 — run the autofix now or scope the ignore to specific paths so the boundary is visible.
P1 — the patch admits it stopped halfway; either land the codemod or don't claim the rule is enforced.
P1 — SPEC-MISSING at the lint-policy boundary; needs owner and kill date.
P1 — file a ticket or do the mechanical rewrite now; otherwise it becomes permanent.
P1 — the discipline is announced and disabled in the same diff; TESTED-NOT-PROVED in policy form.

dissents.topic: Severity of the install.sh minor-version check still permitting 3.7-3.9

positions.position: P1 — the message says >= 3.10 but the predicate accepts 3.7/3.8/3.9; tighten the gate or you ship a half-removed 3.9.
P2 — call it a readability/correctness mismatch worth tightening.
P2 — place-oriented drift between message and predicate.
P2 — small contract drift between docs and code.
P2 — specification and implementation disagree; pick one.

issues.description: default_raise() sentinel and field(default_factory=default_raise) pattern retained as 3.9-compat scaffolding after 3.9 is dropped
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py still defines default_raise() with the comment 'this is just for < 3.10 compatibility' and uses field(default_factory=default_raise) across many request dataclasses. With kw_only=True now universal, required fields can simply omit a default and the dataclass constructor will raise TypeError naturally. Keeping the sentinel weakens the type's invariant — a field appears to have a default-producing factory but in fact raises at call time, which is a runtime trap where the type system could have refused the program. Either delete default_raise and make these fields required, or rewrite the comment with an honest current rationale (e.g., streamable's @dataclass requires every field to have a default).

issues.description: Ruff UP045/UP007/UP035 suppressed wholesale with a bare TODO — contradicts the PR's stated motivation
issues.detail: ruff.toml adds UP045, UP007, UP035 to the global ignore list with the comment 'TODO: Remove these - it's a lot of errors'. These are exactly the Optional[X] -> X | None and Union -> | migration rules that the PR description names as the motivating cleanup for raising the floor to 3.10. A bare TODO with no owner, no issue link, and no kill date freezes the codebase in a mixed type-syntax state and is how style debt becomes permanent. Either land the mechanical codemod now (ruff check --fix --select UP007,UP035,UP045) or scope the ignore to specific paths and reference a tracked issue.

issues.description: Amazon Linux / Rocky install scripts run 'dnf search python3.12' and 'dnf update -y' in CI install step
issues.detail: test-install-scripts.yml now runs 'dnf update -y && dnf search python3.12 && dnf install git python3.12 -y' on both Amazon Linux and Rocky. dnf search is an interactive discovery command whose output is not consumed and not asserted on — pure log noise that looks like debug residue. dnf update -y on every CI run is large unpinned work that churns the image, slows the job, and changes the baseline between runs. The minimum patch should be 'dnf install -y git python3.12'.

issues.description: install.sh version-floor numeric check still permits Python 3.7-3.9 despite '>= 3.10' error message
issues.detail: install.sh prints 'Chia requires Python version >= 3.10 and < 3.13.0' but the guard immediately above remains '[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ]'. So if a user has python3.8 or python3.9 on PATH, the script will march on and try to install with an unsupported interpreter, then fail downstream with a worse error. Tighten the numeric guard to '-lt 10' so the executable check matches the user-visible string. Torvalds rated this P1; others rated it P2.

issues.description: kw_only_dataclass helper removed but expanded into ~15 identical decorator stacks instead of kept as one named concept
issues.detail: The PR deletes the kw_only_dataclass helper and inlines @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) on roughly fifteen classes. The helper carried a real concept (the project-wide convention that streamable request types are frozen kw-only dataclasses) and the rationale string. Replacing one name with fifteen identical decorator stacks is easy-not-simple: each site is familiar, but the concept is now scattered and the next change (say, adding slots=True) touches fifteen places. A one-line wrapper without the version branch is still the right shape. Pike disagrees and treats the removal as a clean win.

issues.description: find_python loop in install.sh still searches bare 'python3' fallback
issues.detail: The shell loop 'for V in 312 3.12 311 3.11 310 3.10 3;' still probes a bare python3, which on Amazon Linux / Rocky / older distros may resolve to 3.9 or earlier. Combined with the stale -lt 7 check, this is how a half-removed 3.9 can ship. Either drop the bare '3' from the search list or tighten the version gate. Also worth a one-line invariant comment stating 'prefer highest available minor, fall back to bare python3 last' and why dual forms (312 and 3.12) coexist.

issues.description: conditions.py drops # pragma: no cover and 3.9 comment without confirming the branch is now covered
issues.detail: Before: 'Something about python 3.9 makes this be not covered but on 3.10+ it is covered' with pragma: no cover on a bare 'continue' inside an elif chain over Condition subclasses. After: bare continue with no annotation. The pragma's removal is correct in spirit, but the change presumes the branch is now exercised by the existing test suite and offers no evidence. Either add/cite a test exercising the branch, or replace the bare continue with an assert/raise so an unknown Condition fails loudly. Right now the branch reads as accidental rather than deliberate.

issues.description: cmd_classes.py option() default semantics shifted from None-fallback to MISSING without audited callers
issues.detail: With 3.9 gone, option() still returns a field with default=kwargs.get('default', MISSING). That is the right answer post-3.10, but the old code distinguished MISSING from None because pre-3.10 dataclasses could not express 'no default with kw_only'. Call sites that used to rely on the None default may now see MISSING and behave differently. The change is reasoned only if all callers were audited for the semantic shift; the diff shows no such audit. A grep is cheap.

issues.description: itertools.pairwise swap is a clean win but unrelated to the stated PR scope
issues.detail: Replacing zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) with itertools.pairwise(ordered) is correct, avoids the O(n) slice allocation, and is only valid on 3.10+. It is, however, an opportunistic cleanup unrelated to 'remove python 3.9 support', and bundling unrelated edits makes the diff harder to bisect and revert. Worth a one-line invariant comment ('every adjacent pair in sorted order satisfies a.before(b)') in the test, and worth a follow-up grep for other zip(xs, xs[1:]) patterns repo-wide.

issues.description: PR bundles multiple concerns: drop 3.9, yum->dnf switch, partial PEP 604 migration, kw_only helper inlining, pairwise swap
issues.detail: The stated change is 'remove Python 3.9 support'. The diff also switches Amazon/Rocky from yum to dnf with added update/search steps, removes the kw_only_dataclass helper and inlines its expansion across ~15 dataclasses, swaps a zip-pairwise idiom for itertools.pairwise, and adds three ruff ignores. Each is defensible individually; bundled, the diff is harder to bisect when something breaks on an Amazon Linux runner weeks later. Split the patch.

issues.description: Possible stragglers: other '# pragma: no cover' or 3.9-justified comments may remain in untouched files
issues.detail: conditions.py drops the 3.9-coverage comment cleanly, but a grep for 'pragma: no cover' and '3.9' across the repo almost certainly still finds stragglers this PR didn't touch. If 3.9 is being closed out, close it out — otherwise the next person doing a python-version bump fights the same ghosts. Worth a sweep across the codebase, not just the files this diff happens to touch.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly on three P1 items: (1) default_raise() and its field(default_factory=default_raise) pattern are stale 3.9-compat scaffolding that should be deleted in favor of real required kw-only fields — every reviewer flagged this; (2) ruff.toml globally ignores UP045/UP007/UP035 with a bare TODO, simultaneously announcing and disabling the Union/Optional migration the PR description claims as motivation; (3) the Amazon/Rocky CI install steps gained a 'dnf search python3.12' probe and a 'dnf update -y' that look like debug residue and slow the matrix. install.sh also still numerically permits 3.7-3.9 while its error message says '>= 3.10' — Torvalds rates that P1, the rest P2. The strongest preserved disagreement is over the kw_only_dataclass helper: Hickey, Torvalds, and Liskov want a thin helper restored to preserve the named project convention; Pike treats the removal as a clean win and Knuth/Dijkstra do not flag it. The mechanical 3.9 removal is competent, but the cleanup is half-done and bundles several unrelated edits.
